analysis_unit_note: the analysis unit is one complete temperature-by-wavelength spectrum or one complete ordered response series; neighbouring wavelengths are correlated scan points, and wavelength-spacing-aware resampling confirmed the boundaries are insensitive to that correlation

findings.title: The composition response reverses sign at a shared optical boundary

robustness.permutation_null_verdict: the plain label-permutation null is NON-INFORMATIVE and is NOT used as a p-value: the composition climatology is rank-1 (PC1 >= 98.9% of level-space variance), so permuted labels reproduce a ~0.9-correlated slope profile about half the time. The informative checks are invariance to label rescaling, single-rung jackknife (<=0.12 nm at 5300/5800 K), random monotone 16-of-31 sub-ladders (median within 0.2 nm), and wavelength resampling

counterevidence: the T=6300 K slice has 3 sign changes, not 1, so 'the' crossover is definition-dependent (first neg->pos = 409.9 nm; a persistence rule gives 434.4 nm; a local-window rule gives 421 nm)
the label-permutation null produces a neg->pos crossing in 80-100% of permutations, so the crossing location alone does not discriminate
flux values carry only 3 significant figures, bounding any resolvable deviation to ~0.2-0.5%
findings.falsification_test: Predict dlogF/dM at 300 nm and at 700 nm for a temperature slice not in this file (e.g. 5000 K or 7000 K). The finding requires the 300 nm slope to stay negative and the 700 nm slope to stay positive.

findings.title: The temperature response reverses sign in the red, and the crossing moves

robustness.null_verdict: SURVIVES.  The crossing location is invariant (0.00 nm) under uniform 5 nm resampling and moves <=11.7 nm under 2x/4x decimation for the claimed 6300/5300 pair.  The 'r<1 at 850 nm' endpoint holds for all 35 metallicity levels under every null (min 0.8553, max 0.9407 across all decimations).  Caveat carried forward from D2: individual 1-2 nm per-metallicity backsteps are below resolution; only the ~20 nm redward trend over the 35 levels is resolved.
robustness.crossing_quantisation_note: many crossings land exactly on 5-nm grid nodes; jitter is of the order of the grid spacing

counterevidence: the redward trend is NOT strictly monotone: backward steps occur, largest ~1.6 nm (at the lowest index), within the sampling-plus-quantisation jitter; an independent refutation therefore judged the metallicity dependence NOT separable from the quantisation noise floor (see output/verification/D2_refutation.json)
the '0.86-0.88 at 850 nm' band is left at both ends by some levels (observed range 0.8559-0.8856)
850 nm is the last grid point: the file cannot show whether the deficit steepens, flattens or turns over beyond it
'order 100x at 180 nm' holds as a median (183x); the ladder spans 85-279x and 7/35 levels fall below 100x
a fitted blackbody pair cannot reproduce the reversal at all: every one of the 35 fitted Planck-pair curves stays above 1 across the whole band, so the reversal requires atmospheric structure
findings.falsification_test: Extend the wavelength axis redward of 850 nm for one temperature pair. The finding requires F(6300)/F(5300) to remain below 1 and the crossing to keep moving redward with increasing metallicity index.

findings.title: The normalized series is a photon-to-energy transform of the 5800 K slice

robustness.registration: the two files' wavelength axes differ (175 vs 176 points) and are index-shifted past index 66; the match was computed after explicit realignment
robustness.calibration_not_circular: fitting the constant on 500-700 nm only, or 400-500 nm only, or 750-850 nm only, reproduces the held-out bands to the same magnitude as inside the fitting window
additional_independent_checks: peak positions: the normalized levels peak at 469.9-479.9 nm, matching the peak of F/wavelength (480 nm at 5300/5800 K), not the peak of F (575-605 nm) -- an independently predicted consequence
ratio consistency: level_k/level_1 reverses sign at 443-447 nm, matching the grid's own T=5800 K composition crossover at 445.8 nm, with no wavelength factor involved

counterevidence: the search is discrete and the winning metallicity for level 3 is nearly degenerate (-0.05 vs 0.00) at the flux quantisation floor
the residual, though small, is at the 3-significant-figure rounding floor, so no finer agreement can be established from this file
the correspondence is a property of the realigned data product; the raw row-index alignment does not match
findings.falsification_test: Obtain the same response series computed at a fourth effective temperature or for an unlisted metallicity index. The finding requires the same transform with only the constant changing per level.

findings.title: The relation breaks below ~330 nm by a discrete, composition-blind factor

factor_ladder_summary.note: the two failing rungs (2.70 nm, 3.50 nm) contain the transition nodes 296.23 and 326.41 nm where the interval itself is ambiguous; every other rung matches 5/step

robustness.registration_shift_is_not_the_cause: the plateau factor stays at 5.00 and the far-UV mean stays at 2.05 under index-shifted, index-unshifted, linear and nearest-neighbour resampling, so the shift is not what produces the deviation

counterevidence: the mechanism's numerator (5 nm) equals the optical grid step, so the data cannot by itself distinguish 'factor = step ratio' from any other quantity proportional to 1/step (see the GAP2 identification test)
the narrow 322-327 nm segment is defined by only 3 points
the far-UV ramp is least accurate (mean relative error ~1.8%)
findings.falsification_test: Re-derive the response series from a flux grid with a uniform wavelength ladder. The artefact explanation requires the sub-330 nm deviation to vanish; a physical explanation requires it to persist.
